products.summary: A wire-free, two-AA combination smoke and CO alarm that reports to the Ring app without a hub. It suits a renter who already uses Ring and wants phone alerts and linked alarms without touching the wiring.
products.renterNote: Runs on 2 AA batteries, so there is nothing to wire; ask your landlord before replacing their alarm, keep the original to refit on move-out, and never remove or disable a working alarm because landlords and fire codes require one. Caveat: it is Ring-centric and the AA batteries are about a one-year job.
pros: Battery-powered with no wiring, and units link wirelessly so one alarm sounds the others
Smoke, CO and low-battery alerts in the Ring app; sources describe the basic alerts as needing no subscription
Dual-sensor design with voice alerts and an 8-minute hush button
cons: Reviewers report occasional Wi-Fi drop-offs and a few unexplained false alarms
Limited smart home reach beyond Ring, no night light, and a premium price versus a basic alarm
facts: Power: 2 AA batteries (non-lithium); Kidde's brochure gives about 1 year before replacement
Sensors: dual-sensor smoke plus CO; meets UL 217 10th Edition and UL 2034 5th Edition
Test/Hush button with an 8-minute hush that resets automatically
Ring app notifications for smoke, CO and low battery, plus voice alerts
Hardwired version is a separate model
products.scoreNote: Wire-free and screw or adhesive mount keep it reversible; Ring-only ecosystem and a roughly yearly AA swap hold back compatibility and value.

praise: Quick setup, about 10 minutes per unit
Reliable Ring app alerts and wire-free linking across floors
complaints: Occasional offline notices and Wi-Fi drops
A few unexplained false alarms and some mounting difficulty

products.summary: Google's named successor to the Nest Protect, in a battery version with voice alerts and app silencing. It suits a Google Home renter who wants a Nest-style alarm without wiring.
products.renterNote: The battery version needs no wiring and ships with batteries installed, so it suits a renter who has the landlord's OK to swap alarms; keep the original to refit on move-out and never leave a room without a working alarm. Caveat: it is Google Home and First Alert app only (no Matter) and it is pricey.
pros: Photoelectric plus electrochemical CO sensing, with voice alerts and silence or test from the app
Setup is quick (batteries pre-installed) and pairs with Google Home and the First Alert app
Fits the Nest Protect mounting bracket and interconnects with First Alert and Nest Protect alarms in Google Home
cons: Not a Matter device and fewer features than the Nest Protect it replaces
Higher price than basic smart alarms, and app alerts need an internet connection
facts: Sensors: photoelectric smoke and electrochemical CO
Available as battery and hardwired versions that can be mixed
Works with the Google Home and First Alert apps; not Matter-enabled
Can reuse the Nest Protect mounting bracket
Interconnect with compatible First Alert alarms and Nest Protect through Google Home
Battery type and life: sources disagree (a Canadian spec sheet lists six CR123A cells and 10-year sensors; one review site claims a 10-year sealed lithium battery); confirm on the box
products.scoreNote: Easy battery install and a reusable bracket score well; premium price and Google-only ecosystem without Matter limit value and compatibility.

praise: Fast three-minute setup with voice prompts
Dual sensors and smooth Google Home integration
complaints: Pricey and fewer features than the Nest Protect
Alerts depend on an internet connection; the hardwired sibling drew weak ratings at one retailer

products.name: Ring Smoke & CO Listener
products.summary: A small device that listens for your existing smoke or CO alarm and sends a phone alert, so you don't replace anything. It suits a renter whose landlord won't allow alarm swaps.
products.renterNote: It sits within 6 inches of the landlord's alarm and changes nothing about it, which fits strict leases; the alarm must be UL listed and 10 years old or less. Caveat: it does not detect smoke or CO itself and you need one per alarm.
pros: Leaves the landlord's alarm untouched and removes in seconds
Newest model uses Amazon Sidewalk with no Ring Alarm base station
Gives a phone alert when an existing alarm sounds
cons: Does not detect smoke or CO itself; roughly one listener per alarm
Sources conflict on subscription needs, the older Z-Wave model needs a Ring Alarm base station, and some owners report it failing to work
facts: Listens for sirens from nearby UL-listed smoke or CO alarms 10 years old or less
Place within 6 inches (ideally 3 inches) of the alarm
Newest model connects over Amazon Sidewalk with no base station; the older Alarm Smoke and CO Listener uses Z-Wave and needs a Ring Alarm base station (battery up to 3 years)
Ring's pages describe optional 24/7 Pro Monitoring with a Ring subscription; check Ring for what plan alerts need
Does not detect fire, smoke or carbon monoxide itself
products.scoreNote: Nothing is removed from the ceiling and it peels off cleanly; one listener per alarm, Ring-only alerts and possible plan costs temper value.

praise: A workable renter fix when the landlord won't replace alarms
complaints: Some owners report it not working and no manual silence
